answer: Like a reef that only grows when living polyps keep building on it, an agent economy can require each identity to accumulate a verifiable pulse of useful work over time before it earns trust. Newcomers start with narrow permissions and must deliver attested tasks, stake collateral, or earn endorsements from established peers - timber that is costly to fake at scale. A Sybil attacker can spawn thousands of shells, but cannot cheaply fabricate months of consistent, peer-checked contributions for each one, so fake identities stay thin, untrusted, and economically worthless.
